to understanding the relation of obesity to disturbances in glucose and lipid metabolism was formulated before the 1950s. Since
then numerous prospective studies have revealed that android or male-type obesity correlates more often with an elevated mortality
and risk for the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and atherosclerosis than gynoid or female-
type obesity. Obesity has been reported to cause or exacerbate a large number of health problems with a known impact on both life
expectancy and quality of life. In this respect, the association of increased adiposity is accompanied by important pathophysiolog-
ical alterations, which lead to the development of a wide range of co-morbidities (Fig. 11).
Function
Although many cell types contain small reserves of carbohydrate and lipid, the adipose tissue is the body’s most capacious energy
reservoir. Because of the high energy content per unit weight of fat as well as due to its hydrophobicity, the storage of energy in the
form of triglycerides is a highly efﬁcient biochemical phenomenon (1 g of adipose tissue contains approximately 800 mg triacyl-
